learning_outcomes.description: Analyse recent developments in research into effectively teaching in inclusive primary classroom environments and the differentiation of teaching in ways that are responsive to the learning strengths and needs of students across the full range of abilities and that take account of the impact on learning of diverse backgrounds (e.g. linguistic, Indigenous, cultural, religious and socio-economic).

Critically reflect on legislative requirements, system policies and processes, positive behaviour supports and teaching strategies that promote student wellbeing and safety, and support participation and learning of all students with a focus on those with disabilities.

Plan challenging learning goals and effectively organise classroom activities for students of diverse backgrounds and across the full range of abilities using age-appropriate curriculum and evidence-based approaches to differentiated teaching strategies.

Explain approaches for interpreting student data and strategies for working appropriately with others, including parents/carers, external professionals and community groups to action an action an individual education plan, modify teaching practices, and report to parents/carers.
Demonstrate clear, fluent, and coherent communication skills consistent with personal, professional and academic conventions.

assessments.assessment_title: Task 1 - Adjusted learning activity development and presentation
assessments.task_description:
In this task, you will work with other students in the course to prepare a presentation of a lesson segment from a full plan that has been designed to meet the learning needs of all students in an inclusive class including those with disability, from diverse backgrounds, Indigenous learners, and with a range of abilities. The lesson plan will be applicable to your learning area and based on the Australian Curriculum.

Using the principles of Universal Design for Learning, your group will plan a 40-minute lesson including teaching that support student participation (including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students), as well as strategies for assessing what students know or are able to do as a result of the lesson.

In addition to the general planning for all, you will plan learning adjustments based on a learning need as specified by the Nationally Consistent Collection of Data categories (Physical, Sensory, Cognitive or Social/Emotional), indicating appropriate adjustments for teaching and assessing a student with that need.

Presentation 30%:

  • lesson plan (individual or group response)
  • presentation of an activity from the lesson plan (up to 20 minutes)


Individual response 20%:

  • overview and background
  • narrative review of current research literature
  • justification of adjustments


Microsoft Copilot is the generative AI tool approved by UQ, and the only AI tool that is permitted for use in this assessment. Students may not use any other AI tool while working on this assessment.

Details of the format for the group presentation and the individual written response will be provided on the course Blackboard site.

assessments.assessment_title: Task 2 - Case study: Response to scenario
assessments.task_description:
This is a culminating task where you will build on your understandings of building inclusive classrooms by documenting preparations for a meeting with parents.

Microsoft Copilot is the generative AI tool approved by UQ, and the only AI tool that is permitted for use in this assessment. Students may not use any other AI tool while working on this assessment.

Scenario:

Two weeks into the new school year, the parents of a student in your year 9 class have asked to meet with you to discuss how you will accommodate their child’s learning needs as specified in the Individual Education Plan[1] (IEP).

In this task, you will document your preparation for the meeting, including the following:

1. Background (suggested two A4 pages)

  • A summary of the relevant legislation and policy documents, and a teacher’s legal obligations, related to this scenario. (Choose a jurisdiction where you plan to teach).
  • A plan of adjustments to be made based on learning, assessment, and behaviour as appropriate to the student’s needs. Justify your plan based on research evidence and subject matter expertise.
  • An indication of the assessment data (formative and summative) you would study prior to the meeting to provide background on the student’s progress.
  • An overview of your investigation of applicable external professional (e.g., allied health professionals) and community representatives including professional support networks, such as disability associations, and other community groups for extending your personal professional knowledge and practice. 
  • A brief summary of relevant research evidence identifying how to effectively engage with families as partners in promoting learning appropriate to the student’s stage of learning.

 

2. A plan for the meeting (suggested two A4 pages)

  • Location, timing, seating arrangement, refreshments etc.
  • Introductions – opportunity for parents to indicate what they wish to gain from the meeting.
  • How you will work with parents/carers over the year, including considerations of sensitivity, confidentiality, seeking their input and advice, and how you intend to collaborate with them throughout the year. You may wish to consider engagement strategies, such as the use of two-way positive communication, collaborative planning and problem-solving, and how you will use light-touch learning updates (e.g. brief, regular updates), among other approaches.
  • Explanation of learning adjustments applicable to your subject area in response to the student’s IEP.
  • Explanation of reasonable adjustments planned for assessment, responding to the IEP.
  • Explanation of your plan for the student’s wellbeing and safety, including positive behaviour support processes (Tier 1, 2 or 3, as applicable).

 

3. Follow up (suggested up to one A4 page)

  • Recording of the conversation.
  • Further meetings.
  • Reporting to others.


[1] Individual Education Plan is internationally recognised terminology. Local jurisdictions may use different terminology e.g. personalised learning plans.

learning_activities.topic:
Week 1 - Embracing inclusive practice

Summary

This first week's activities set the context for this course. It introduces students to the concept of inclusion and begins the work of developing an evidence base for practice. Introduction to Universal Design for Learning (UDL) establishes an approach to planning learning and assessment activities to support the majority of learners. Some learners need more than UDL, requiring learning adjustments. Approaches such as Learning Year Level Adjusted Curriculum will be introduced. Underpinning all this work is a research evidence base. Students will learn how to access the research evidence and prepare a narrative literature review.

Session 1: Embracing inclusive practice

  • Introductions 
  • Defining inclusion
  • Inclusive language

You are introduced to the research evidence supporting highly effective inclusive practices, including systematic reviews of evidence for inclusive practice and how these practices benefit all students, including those with additional needs or from disadvantaged backgrounds (CC 4.4.1, 4.4.2 – taught)

Session 2: Universal Design for Learning (CC 4.4.2 – taught). 

Session 3: Finding the evidence

• Searching the library catalogue

In this session, you are taught to use search techniques to select peer-reviewed research literature identifying research evidence for inclusive practice. You then practise these skills by identifying relevant research literature and discussing the findings in groups. This leads to Task 1 where practical strategies are planned into a lesson to meet specific learning support needs and to Task 2 where your understanding of the evidence is assessed (CC 4.4.1, 4.4.3 – practised). You also work through the training modules about the Disability Standards for Education on the NCCD website https://www.nccd.edu.au/professional-learning/disability-standards-education-pre-service-teachers . This leads to Task 2 where this knowledge is assessed (CC 4.4.2 – practised)

Session 4: Year level adjusted curriculum

Session 5: Assessing learning

  • UDL
  • Formative & summative
  • Making adjustments

Assessment strategies that promote learning are taught in this session. Adjustments to assessment are a legal requirement for students with disabilities and you are taught to plan these adjustments. This leads to Task 1 where formative assessment is required to be designed into the lesson plan. To support this seminar, professional learning resources from AITSL, ACARA and Assessment Guides are used, in addition to textbook references (CC 4.4.3 – taught). 

In this session, you collaborate to plan options for lesson features to support diverse learning needs using the UDL framework. In addition, you practise designing learning adjustments for students with individual education plans requiring supports beyond what is provided through UDL (CC 4.4.3 – practised).

Session 6: Technology in the classroom (CC 4.4.2 – taught). 

You share the accessibility features of a technological device (e.g. a smart phone) in presentations to your tutorial group. You also investigate the AAC (Augmentative and Alternative Communication) devices available through the UQ library and from resources centres e.g. Vision Australia (CC 4.4.3 – practised).


Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

learning_activities.topic:
Week 2 - Understanding the legislative context - Evidence for Inclusive Education

Summary

The education of students with disabilities is underpinned by international charters, Australian and state legislation and local policies. This week covers legal frameworks for inclusion, the research evidence for the effectiveness of inclusive education, and Australia's Nationally Consistent Collection of Data scheme.

Our legal obligations are important. The purpose is to ensure all learners can enjoy their right to a quality education in safe, supportive environments. Therefore, this week, we also cover Educational Quality of Life, student well-being, trauma informed practices, and approaches to supporting behaviour for learning.

Specific approaches to support learners with language, literacy and numeracy development are covered.

Session 1: Evidence for Inclusive education

  • for students with disabilities
  • students without disabilities (CC 4.4.2 – taught). 

Session 2: Understanding the legislative context

  • International charters
  • Australian law (DDA; DSE)
  • Policies e.g. EQ Inclusive Ed policy

Session 3

  • Complete NCCD modules (4.4.2 – taught)

Session 4

  • Educational Quality of Life
  • Student well-being
  • Trauma-informed practice You discuss and practise strategies for supporting the wellbeing of students. These strategies are modelled by tutors and explicitly explained (CC 4.4.2 – taught; CC 4.4.3 – practised).

Session 5: Supporting behaviour for learning.

Students learn the psychological basis to Positive Behaviour Support strategies and explore how to implement these practices in classrooms. These assist teachers to establish and maintain classroom environments for learning. Students learn to look to the motivation behind behaviours to support students with diverse needs (CC 4.4.3 – taught).

You discuss antecedents and consequences of common classroom behaviours to identify motivations behind the observed behaviours. You then consider responses teachers might make to the situation to assist learners to develop positive behaviours for learning (CC 4.4.3 – practised).

Session 6: Language and Literacy

In this seminar, you learn evidence-based approaches for supporting students with language disorders and specific learning difficulties (CC 4.4.3 – taught).

This seminar focuses on developmental language disorder and other language learning difficulties. You practise strategies, such as making adjustments to the language level of texts, to support learners in secondary classrooms (CC 4.4.3 – practised).


Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03

learning_activities.topic:
Week 3 - Working with others

Summary: Presentations

Teachers work with many others, including other teaching staff, allied professionals e.g. therapists, teacher aides and families. Communities of Practice (COP) or Professional Learning Communities (PLC) are helpful organisational structures which will be introduced this week.

Teachers work in teams, often as the leader. When a student with an individual learning plan is in the class, many people may be involved in the community of practice. These could be teacher aides, specialist teachers, therapists, parents and learning support teams. This module will explore ways of building positive relationships, including running meetings.

Transitions involve working with others and are an important aspect of the work of teachers as students move into, between and out of school contexts.

Session 1, 2, 4: Task 1 presentations

Session 3: Individual Education Plans

In this seminar, you are taught how individual education plans are developed by schools and the role classroom teachers take in providing input into subject specific requirements of the plan, and how to engage with families who may be unfamiliar with the secondary school content (CC 4.3.2 – taught).

Session 5

In this seminar, you are taught to support learners at various levels of attainment, based on Learning Year Level Adjusted Curriculum, supported by the research literature (CC 4.4.3 – taught).

Panel discussion

  • Parent
  • Head of learning support – primary & secondary
  • Disability advocate

You hear from a panel of experts, comprising a head of learning support, a disability expert (relevant to the disability focus of the IEP) and a parent, to discuss the context of meeting with a parent. You are encouraged to ask questions about how to encourage family engagement in learning. You can also test out ideas you might have for when they are teaching (CC 4.3.2 – taught). The teachers share strategies that are successful for them in supporting the learning of students with disability. The disability expert also teaches evidence informed strategies (CC 4.4.3 – taught).

In this seminar you practise strategies for promoting behaviours that support learning in a classroom. You practise approaches for working with families when issues arise. (CC 4.3.2 – practised).

Session 6: Role-play a meeting with parents (CC 4.3.1 – taught)

In this session, you practice engaging with parents in a meeting. This builds towards your response for Task 2 where you prepare a plan for the meeting. This practice involves taking part in role plays where you take turns to adopt the roles of parent, teacher or student (CC 4.3.1, 4.3.2 – practised).

Session 7 

  • Building a professional learning community
  • Working with teacher aides (CC 4.3.1, 4.3.2 – taught)
  • This session involves practising strategies for working with teams in classrooms (CC 4.3.2 – practised)

Session 8

  • Partnering with families
  • Community organisations (CC 4.3.1, 4.3.2 – taught) 

This session involves practising strategies for building relationships with families. You practise how to collaborate with others, including families (CC 4.3.2 – practised) You also learn to judge the quality of the sources (CC 4.4.3 – practised).

Session 9

• Conclusion and next steps


Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
